NASB.1: Now Saul told Jonathan his son and all his servants to put David to death. But Jonathan, Saul's son, greatly delighted in David.
NASB.2: So Jonathan told David saying, 'Saul my father is seeking to put you to death. Now therefore, please be on guard in the morning, and stay in a secret place and hide yourself.
NASB.3: 'I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak with my father about you; if I find out anything, then I will tell you.'
NASB.4: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him, 'Do not let the king sin against his servant David, since he has not sinned against you, and since his deeds [have been] very beneficial to you.
NASB.5: 'For he took his life in his hand and struck the Philistine, and the LORD brought about a great deliverance for all Israel; you saw [it] and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death without a cause?'
NASB.6: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul vowed, 'As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.'
NASB.7: Then Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as formerly.
NASB.8: When there was war again, David went out and fought with the Philistines and defeated them with great slaughter, so that they fled before him.
NASB.9: Now there was an evil spirit from the LORD on Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing [the harp] with [his] hand.
NASB.10: Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away out of Saul's presence, so that he stuck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
NASB.11: Then Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him, in order to put him to death in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him, saying, 'If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death.'
NASB.12: So Michal let David down through a window, and he went out and fled and escaped.
NASB.13: Michal took the household idol and laid [it] on the bed, and put a quilt of goats' [hair] at its head, and covered [it] with clothes.
NASB.14: When Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, 'He is sick.'
NASB.15: Then Saul sent messengers to see David, saying, 'Bring him up to me on his bed, that I may put him to death.'
NASB.16: When the messengers entered, behold, the household idol [was] on the bed with the quilt of goats' [hair] at its head.
NASB.17: So Saul said to Michal, 'Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?' And Michal said to Saul, 'He said to me, 'Let me go! Why should I put you to death?''
NASB.18: Now David fled and escaped and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed in Naioth.
NASB.19: It was told Saul, saying, 'Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.'
NASB.20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David, but when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing [and] presiding over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul; and they also prophesied.
NASB.21: When it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. So Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they also prophesied.
NASB.22: Then he himself went to Ramah and came as far as the large well that is in Secu; and he asked and said, 'Where are Samuel and David?' And [someone] said, 'Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.'
NASB.23: He proceeded there to Naioth in Ramah; and the Spirit of God came upon him also, so that he went along prophesying continually until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
NASB.24: He also stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Samuel and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, 'Is Saul also among the prophets?'

ESV.1: And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David.
ESV.2: And Jonathan told David, “Saul my father seeks to kill you. Therefore be on your guard in the morning. Stay in a secret place and hide yourself.
ESV.3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak to my father about you. And if I learn anything I will tell you.”
ESV.4: And Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him, “Let not the king sin against his servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and because his deeds have brought good to you.
ESV.5: For he took his life in his hand and he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it, and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?”
ESV.6: And Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan. Saul swore, “As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death.”
ESV.7: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan reported to him all these things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.
ESV.8: And there was war again. And David went out and fought with the Philistines and struck them with a great blow, so that they fled before him.
ESV.9: Then a harmful spirit from the LORD came upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And David was playing the lyre.
ESV.10: And Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he eluded Saul, so that he struck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
ESV.11: Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him, that he might kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you do not escape with your life tonight, tomorrow you will be killed.”
ESV.12: So Michal let David down through the window, and he fled away and escaped.
ESV.13: Michal took an image  and laid it on the bed and put a pillow of goats' hair at its head and covered it with the clothes.
ESV.14: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, “He is sick.”
ESV.15: Then Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may kill him.”
ESV.16: And when the messengers came in, behold, the image was in the bed, with the pillow of goats' hair at its head.
ESV.17: Saul said to Michal, “Why have you deceived me thus and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?” And Michal answered Saul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go. Why should I kill you?’”
ESV.18: Now David fled and escaped, and he came to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and lived at Naioth.
ESV.19: And it was told Saul, “Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.”
ESV.20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David, and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as head over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
ESV.21: When it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they also prophesied.
ESV.22: Then he himself went to Ramah and came to the great well that is in Secu. And he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” And one said, “Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.”
ESV.23: And he went there to Naioth in Ramah. And the Spirit of God came upon him also, and as he went he prophesied until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
ESV.24: And he too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Samuel and lay naked all that day and all that night. Thus it is said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

NKJV.1: Now Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill David; but Jonathan, Saul’s son, delighted greatly in David.
NKJV.2: So Jonathan told David, saying, “My father Saul seeks to kill you. Therefore please be on your guard until morning, and stay in a secret place and hide.
NKJV.3: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak with my father about you. Then what I observe, I will tell you.”
NKJV.4: Thus Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father, and said to him, “Let not the king sin against his servant, against David, because he has not sinned against you, and because his works have been very good toward you.
NKJV.5: For he took his life in his hands and killed the Philistine, and the LORD brought about a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then will you sin against innocent blood, to kill David without a cause?”
NKJV.6: So Saul heeded the voice of Jonathan, and Saul swore, “As the LORD lives, he shall not be killed.”
NKJV.7: Then Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these things. So Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past.
NKJV.8: And there was war again; and David went out and fought with the Philistines, and struck them with a mighty blow, and they fled from him.
NKJV.9: Now the distressing spirit from the LORD came upon Saul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand. And David was playing music with his hand.
NKJV.10: Then Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away from Saul’s presence; and he drove the spear into the wall. So David fled and escaped that night.
NKJV.11: Saul also sent messengers to David’s house to watch him and to kill him in the morning. And Michal, David’s wife, told him, saying, “If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be killed.”
NKJV.12: So Michal let David down through a window. And he went and fled and escaped.
NKJV.13: And Michal took an image and laid it in the bed, put a cover of goats’ hair for his head, and covered it with clothes.
NKJV.14: So when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, “He is sick.”
NKJV.15: Then Saul sent the messengers back to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may kill him.”
NKJV.16: And when the messengers had come in, there was the image in the bed, with a cover of goats’ hair for his head.
NKJV.17: Then Saul said to Michal, “Why have you deceived me like this, and sent my enemy away, so that he has escaped?” And Michal answered Saul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I kill you?’ ”
NKJV.18: So David fled and escaped, and went to Samuel at Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed in Naioth.
NKJV.19: Now it was told Saul, saying, “Take note, David is at Naioth in Ramah!”
NKJV.20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David. And when they saw the group of prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as leader over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
NKJV.21: And when Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. Then Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also.
NKJV.22: Then he also went to Ramah, and came to the great well that is at Sechu. So he asked, and said, “Where are Samuel and David?” And someone said, “Indeed they are at Naioth in Ramah.”
NKJV.23: So he went there to Naioth in Ramah. Then the Spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on and prophesied until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
NKJV.24: And he also stripped off his clothes and prophesied before Samuel in like manner, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Therefore they say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

NLT.1: Saul now urged his servants and his son Jonathan to assassinate David. But Jonathan, because of his strong affection for David,
NLT.2: told him what his father was planning. “Tomorrow morning,” he warned him, “you must find a hiding place out in the fields.
NLT.3: I’ll ask my father to go out there with me, and I’ll talk to him about you. Then I’ll tell you everything I can find out.”
NLT.4: The next morning Jonathan spoke with his father about David, saying many good things about him. “The king must not sin against his servant David,” Jonathan said. “He’s never done anything to harm you. He has always helped you in any way he could.
NLT.5: Have you forgotten about the time he risked his life to kill the Philistine giant and how the LORD brought a great victory to all Israel as a result? You were certainly happy about it then. Why should you murder an innocent man like David? There is no reason for it at all!”
NLT.6: So Saul listened to Jonathan and vowed, “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be killed.”
NLT.7: Afterward Jonathan called David and told him what had happened. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in the court as before.
NLT.8: War broke out again after that, and David led his troops against the Philistines. He attacked them with such fury that they all ran away.
NLT.9: But one day when Saul was sitting at home, with spear in hand, the tormenting spirit from the LORD suddenly came upon him again. As David played his harp,
NLT.10: Saul hurled his spear at David. But David dodged out of the way, and leaving the spear stuck in the wall, he fled and escaped into the night.
NLT.11: Then Saul sent troops to watch David’s house. They were told to kill David when he came out the next morning. But Michal, David’s wife, warned him, “If you don’t escape tonight, you will be dead by morning.”
NLT.12: So she helped him climb out through a window, and he fled and escaped.
NLT.13: Then she took an idol and put it in his bed, covered it with blankets, and put a cushion of goat’s hair at its head.
NLT.14: When the troops came to arrest David, she told them he was sick and couldn’t get out of bed.
NLT.15: But Saul sent the troops back to get David. He ordered, “Bring him to me in his bed so I can kill him!”
NLT.16: But when they came to carry David out, they discovered that it was only an idol in the bed with a cushion of goat’s hair at its head.
NLT.17: “Why have you betrayed me like this and let my enemy escape?” Saul demanded of Michal. “I had to,” Michal replied. “He threatened to kill me if I didn’t help him.”
NLT.18: So David escaped and went to Ramah to see Samuel, and he told him all that Saul had done to him. Then Samuel took David with him to live at Naioth.
NLT.19: When the report reached Saul that David was at Naioth in Ramah,
NLT.20: he sent troops to capture him. But when they arrived and saw Samuel leading a group of prophets who were prophesying, the Spirit of God came upon Saul’s men, and they also began to prophesy.
NLT.21: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent other troops, but they, too, prophesied! The same thing happened a third time.
NLT.22: Finally, Saul himself went to Ramah and arrived at the great well in Secu. “Where are Samuel and David?” he demanded. “They are at Naioth in Ramah,” someone told him.
NLT.23: But on the way to Naioth in Ramah the Spirit of God came even upon Saul, and he, too, began to prophesy all the way to Naioth!
NLT.24: He tore off his clothes and lay naked on the ground all day and all night, prophesying in the presence of Samuel. The people who were watching exclaimed, “What? Is even Saul a prophet?”

AMP.1: Now Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David, but Jonathan, Saul's son, greatly delighted in David.
AMP.2: So he told David, "Saul my father is seeking to kill you. Now then, please be on guard in the morning, and stay in a secret place and hide yourself.
AMP.3: As for me, I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak with my father about you, and if I learn anything, then I will tell you."
AMP.4: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father and said to him, "May the king not sin against his servant David, since he has not sinned against you, and since his deeds have been very beneficial to you.
AMP.5: For he took his life in his hand and killed the Philistine, and the LORD brought about a great victory for all Israel; you saw it and rejoiced. Why then would you sin against innocent blood by killing David without a cause?"
AMP.6: Saul listened to Jonathan and swore [an oath], "As the LORD lives, he shall not be put to death."
AMP.7: So Jonathan called David and told him all these things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence [serving him] as previously.
AMP.8: Then there was war again, and David went out and fought with the Philistines and defeated them with a great slaughter, and they fled before him.
AMP.9: Then an evil spirit from the LORD came on Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing the harp with his hand.
AMP.10: Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he escaped from Saul's presence, so that Saul only stuck the spear into the wall. Then David fled and escaped that night.
AMP.11: Then Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch for him, so that he might kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him, "If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be killed."
AMP.12: So Michal let David down through the window, and he fled and escaped.
AMP.13: And Michal took the household idol and laid it on the bed, put a pillow of goats' hair at its head, and covered it with clothes.
AMP.14: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, "He is sick."
AMP.15: Then Saul sent the messengers [again] to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me on his bed [if necessary], so that I may kill him."
AMP.16: When the messengers came in, there was the household idol on the bed with a quilt of goats' hair at its head.
AMP.17: Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?" Michal answered Saul, "He said to me, 'Let me go! Why should I kill you?'"
AMP.18: So David fled and escaped and came to Samuel at Ramah, and told him everything that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed in Naioth.
AMP.19: Saul was told, "David is at Naioth in Ramah."
AMP.20: Then Saul sent messengers to take David; but when they saw the group of prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing and presiding over them, the Spirit of God came on the messengers of Saul; and they also prophesied.
AMP.21: When Saul was informed, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. So Saul sent messengers again, the third time, and they prophesied as well.
AMP.22: Then Saul went to Ramah himself and came to the great well that is in Secu; and he asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" And he was told, "They are at Naioth [with the prophets] in Ramah."
AMP.23: So he went on to Naioth in Ramah; and the Spirit of God came upon him too, and he went along continually prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
AMP.24: He also took off his [royal] robes [and armor] and prophesied before Samuel and lay down naked all that day and night. So they say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

CSB17.1: Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. <sup>ⓙ</sup> But Saul’s son Jonathan liked David very much, <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.2: so he told him: “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning and hide in a secret place and stay there.
CSB17.3: I’ll go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are and talk to him about you. When I see what he says, I’ll tell you.” <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.4: Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul. He said to him: “The king should not sin against his servant David. <sup>ⓜ</sup> He hasn’t sinned against you; in fact, his actions have been a great advantage to you.
CSB17.5: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, <sup>ⓝ</sup> and the LORD brought about a great victory for all Israel. <sup>ⓐ</sup> You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.6: Saul listened to Jonathan’s advice and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be killed.”
CSB17.7: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these words. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he served him as he did before. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.8: When war broke out again, David went out and fought against the Philistines. He defeated them with such great force that they fled from him.
CSB17.9: Now an evil spirit sent from the LORD <sup>ⓓ</sup> came on Saul as he was sitting in his palace holding a spear. <sup>ⓔ</sup> David was playing the lyre, <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.10: and Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear. <sup>ⓖ</sup> As the spear struck the wall, David eluded Saul, ran away, and escaped that night.
CSB17.11: Saul sent agents to David’s house to watch for him and kill him in the morning. <sup>ⓗ</sup> But his wife Michal <sup>ⓘ</sup> warned David, “If you don’t escape tonight, you will be dead tomorrow!”
CSB17.12: So she lowered David from the window, and he fled and escaped. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.13: Then Michal took the household idol and put it on the bed, placed some goat hair on its head, and covered it with a garment.
CSB17.14: When Saul sent agents to seize David, Michal said, “He’s sick.” <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.15: Saul sent the agents back to see David and said, “Bring him on his bed so I can kill him.”
CSB17.16: When the agents arrived, to their surprise, the household idol was on the bed with some goat hair on its head.
CSB17.17: Saul asked Michal, “Why did you deceive me like this? You sent my enemy away, and he has escaped!” She answered him, “He said to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I kill you? ’”
CSB17.18: So David fled and escaped and went to Samuel at Ramah <sup>ⓛ</sup> and told him everything Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel left and stayed at Naioth. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.19: When it was reported to Saul that David was at Naioth in Ramah,
CSB17.20: he sent agents to seize David. <sup>ⓝ</sup> However, when they saw the group of prophets prophesying <sup>ⓐ</sup> with Samuel leading them, the Spirit of God came on Saul’s agents, and they also started prophesying.
CSB17.21: When they reported to Saul, he sent other agents, and they also began prophesying. <sup>ⓑ</sup> So Saul tried again and sent a third group of agents, and even they began prophesying.
CSB17.22: Then Saul himself went to Ramah. He came to the large cistern at Secu and asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Naioth in Ramah,” someone said.
CSB17.23: So he went to Naioth in Ramah. The Spirit of God also came on him, <sup>ⓒ</sup> and as he walked along, he prophesied until he entered Naioth in Ramah.
CSB17.24: Saul then removed his clothes and also prophesied before Samuel; he collapsed and lay naked <sup>ⓓ</sup> all that day and all that night. That is why they say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?” <sup>ⓔ</sup>

MSG.1: Saul called his son Jonathan together with his servants and ordered them to kill David. But because Jonathan treasured David,
MSG.2: he went and warned him: "My father is looking for a way to kill you. Here's what you are to do. Tomorrow morning, hide and stay hidden.
MSG.3: I'll go out with my father into the field where you are hiding. I'll talk about you with my father and we'll see what he says. Then I'll report back to you."
MSG.4: Jonathan brought up David with his father, speaking well of him. "Please," he said to his father, "don't attack David. He hasn't wronged you, has he? And just look at all the good he has done!
MSG.5: He put his life on the line when he killed the Philistine. What a great victory God gave Israel that day! You were there. You saw it and were on your feet applauding with everyone else. So why would you even think of sinning against an innocent person, killing David for no reason whatever?"
MSG.6: Saul listened to Jonathan and said, "You're right. As God lives, David lives. He will not be killed."
MSG.7: Jonathan sent for David and reported to him everything that was said. Then he brought David back to Saul and everything was as it was before.
MSG.8: War broke out again and David went out to fight Philistines. He beat them badly, and they ran for their lives.
MSG.9: But then a black mood from God settled over Saul and took control of him. He was sitting at home, his spear in his hand, while David was playing music.
MSG.10: Suddenly, Saul tried to skewer David with his spear, but David ducked. The spear stuck in the wall and David got away. It was night.
MSG.11: Saul sent men to David's house to stake it out and then, first thing in the morning, to kill him. But Michal, David's wife, told him what was going on. "Quickly now—make your escape tonight. If not, you'll be dead by morning!"
MSG.12: She let him out of a window, and he made his escape.
MSG.13: Then Michal took a dummy god and put it in the bed, placed a wig of goat's hair on its head, and threw a quilt over it.
MSG.14: When Saul's men arrived to get David, she said, "He's sick in bed."
MSG.15: Saul sent his men back, ordering them, "Bring him, bed and all, so I can kill him."
MSG.16: When the men entered the room, all they found in the bed was the dummy god with its goat-hair wig!
MSG.17:
Saul stormed at Michal: "How could you play tricks on me like this? You sided with my enemy, and now he's gotten away!"
Michal said, "He threatened me. He said, 'Help me out of here or I'll kill you.' "
MSG.18: David made good his escape and went to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel withdrew to the privacy of Naioth.
MSG.19: Saul was told, "David's at Naioth in Ramah."
MSG.20: He immediately sent his men to capture him. They saw a band of prophets prophesying with Samuel presiding over them. Before they knew it, the Spirit of God was on them, too, and they were ranting and raving right along with the prophets!
MSG.21: That was reported back to Saul, and he dispatched more men. They, too, were soon prophesying. So Saul tried a third time—a third set of men—and they ended up mindlessly raving as well!
MSG.22:
Fed up, Saul went to Ramah himself. He came to the big cistern at Secu and inquired, "Where are Samuel and David?"
A bystander said, "Over at Naioth in Ramah."
MSG.23: As he headed out for Naioth in Ramah, the Spirit of God was on him, too. All the way to Naioth he was caught up in a babbling trance!
MSG.24: He ripped off his clothes and lay there rambling gibberish before Samuel for a day and a night, stretched out naked. People are still talking about it: "Saul among the prophets! Who would have guessed?"

NET.1: Then Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Saul’s son Jonathan liked David very much.
